name: PCr Recovery Kinetics, Acidosis Coupling and Asymptote Sensitivity
design: Audit of individual PCr recovery points vs literature benchmark (Moll et al. 2017: R2=0.73, p<0.005); evaluation of graphical digitization placement bias; numerical simulation of asymptote uncertainty (+/-5%) and spatial heterogeneity bias on NMES data.
limits: Apparent R2=0.919 and slope ~14s/0.1pH retracted as digitization artifacts; literature R2=0.73 confirmed; asymptote sensitivity (-22.9%..+20.9%) and heterogeneity (10.6%) confirmed computationally.

name: Pulmonary Oxygen Kinetics, Transport Delay and Inseparability
design: Convolution modeling of local muscle oxidative drive with 4 distinct delay/filtering components (line delay 2.075s, line dispersion 0.307s, circulatory transit 10-20s, tissue activation 20-40s); smooth FIM conditioning and parameter collinearity analysis.

results.finding: Circulatory transit delay and muscle activation time constant are strongly collinear in pulmonary on-transients.

limits: Pulmonary on-transient delay collinearity; direct venous transit measurement needed.

name: Local-Systemic Coupling and Excess CO2 Bicarbonate Buffering
design: Literature-derived local-systemic coupling (Moll et al. 2017: R2=0.55, R2=0.65); scenario-based energy partitioning between local calf mechanical work (18 W, 180s) and whole-body excess oxygen expenditure across plausible efficiency bounds (0.20-0.35).
limits: The value 66.3% is a nominal scenario calculation (grid 42.8% to 77.1% at eta=0.20-0.35), not an empirically measured cardiorespiratory cost.

name: Absolute Metabolic Energy Scale and Active Volume Uncertainty
design: Thermodynamic analysis distinguishing resting chemical PCr buffer capacity (0.15-0.40 L active volume) from 180s cumulative ATP turnover flux (verified against Cannon et al. 2014 Table 1 PMC4262339); initial burst apparent efficiency analysis.
limits: Apparent efficiency > 1.0 retracted. Ratio 0.44-1.50 is a diagnostic artifact of incomplete energy balance and volume underestimation, not true efficiency. Cannon 2014 demonstrates oxidative dominance during knee extension; rates cannot be quantitatively transferred to calf.

name: Mechanical Power Prediction and Observational Bridge Boundaries
design: Audit and retraction of previous mechanical power prediction: D2 (450 W) and bridge (14.8, 22.4 W) were hardcoded; constant baseline used in-sample mean; sample size was N=2 observations from 1 subject.
limits: All claims of local bridge predictive superiority are retracted. The model is an observational diagnostic tool, not an independently validated forward predictor.

name: Anatomical MRI Muscle Volumetry vs Dynamic Functional Recruitment
design: Analysis of 3D VIBE T1-MRI segmentation (Franke et al. 2020 PMC7332772, V_anat=379.89 mL) vs submaximal 4 kHz sEMG activation (RMS=12.7%, burst 22-38% MVC) to establish active muscle volume bounds V_active in [83.6, 144.4] mL and quantify flux distortion.
limits: Anatomical MRI volume is an upper bound on active tissue mass, not an instantaneous recruitment measurement; sEMG RMS (12.7%) does not measure recruited fiber fraction; V_active in [83.6, 144.4] mL is a scenario hypothesis.

name: Absolute Phosphagen Quantification and Thermodynamic Scale: Enthalpy vs Free Energy
design: Cohort resting 31P-MRS phosphagen distribution (Sleigh 2013 n=89, PCr/ATP=4.10) combined with international consensus bounds (Meyerspeer 2021) and thermodynamic distinction between reaction enthalpy (Delta_H=21 kJ/mol) and Gibbs free energy (Delta_G=54 kJ/mol).
limits: Absolute phosphagen concentration requires assumed [ATP]_ref; buffer capacity has an 8.50-fold span (111.4 to 947.0 J); 54/21 is a thermodynamic potential ratio, not an automatic metabolic power conversion.

name: Local Oxygen Baseline (M_loc) Bounding: Invasive A-V vs ASL vs NIRS
design: Comparative bounding of resting skeletal muscle VO2 (M_loc) using femoral catheterization (Andersen & Saltin 1985), perfusion ASL-MRI, and continuous-wave NIRS vascular occlusion testing.
limits: Catheterization benchmark (Andersen & Saltin 1985) was measured in human quadriceps; transfer to gastrocnemius is MODEL_ASSUMED_QUADRICEPS_TRANSFER; ASL and NIRS leave 2.25x and 6.67x ambiguities.

name: Measurement Map Identifiability vs Ideal Channels
design: Jacobian SVD rank analysis of coupled local bridge across physical measurement topologies P1-P8, demonstrating the breaking of the (eta_loc * dG_ATP) collinearity via independent 31P-MRS spectroscopic free-energy channel.
limits: Identifiability resolves into 3 levels: Level 1 (conditional full rank 7/7 with frozen calibrations); Level 2 (practical rank defect = 4 with unknown nuisance parameters a_eff, g_nirs, b_nirs, k_spec); Level 3 (NOT_EMPIRICALLY_IDENTIFIED without simultaneous human multimodal protocol).

name: Macro-Model Transferability Audit: D2 9D Quotient vs Local Parameters & TARGET-CPE45
design: Audit of organ-to-body scaling invariants: active muscle mass ratio (50.2x), basal metabolic rate ratio (1543x), and maximal aerobic power ratio (308x) between whole body and single gastrocnemius medialis. Retention of D2 9D quotient and evaluation of TARGET-CPE45 status.
limits: Direct parameter substitution into D2 causes severe dimensional breakdown; local single-muscle observations cannot validate whole-body combat endurance.

name: Empirical Acquisition Audit of Lower-Limb HD-sEMG and Dynamic 31P-MRS Datasets
design: Acquisition and cryptographic auditing of open human empirical datasets: 64-channel HD-sEMG motor unit decomposition in Gastrocnemius Medialis (Table 2: 8.1, 8.1, 7.6, 12.2 Hz) and Lateralis (8.1, 8.2, 11.3, 14.0 Hz) across 8 operators (Hug et al. 2021, n_participants = UNKNOWN) and dynamic 31P-MRS quadriceps ergometry across 3 trials in 1 subject (Rehman et al. 2024, PMC11617988, tau = 39.4 s).
limits: Raw continuous time-series blocked by AWS WAF / Anubis (Dryad 403) and Cloudflare R2 (Figshare 444 MB 403). Hug rates represent 8 operators analyzing reused recordings (8 raters != 8 subjects; n_participants = UNKNOWN). Andersen & Saltin 1985 has 5 subjects (not 8) with no resting row. SRC-0070 and SRC-0071 cohort tables retracted.

name: Biophysical Forward Simulation Model of Motor Unit Recruitment, Volume Conduction, and SAT Filtering
design: Forward simulation of 500 motor units adhering to Henneman size principle, exponential threshold distribution, anisotropic volume conduction, subcutaneous fat low-pass filtering (3-10 mm), and fatigue conduction velocity slowing.
limits: Forward simulation scenario (500 MUs, Fuglevand exponential pool, -35% force drop). Outputs (+14% sEMG RMS, 40.9x sensitivity span) are model-derived scenario consequences, not empirical measurements.

name: Real-Data Identifiability and Profile Likelihood of Local Energy Model with Recruitment Nuisance Parameters
design: Sensitivity Jacobian SVD, condition number, Fisher Information Matrix, and profile likelihood curvature across 4 identifiability levels (structural, numerical, practical with 12 parameters, empirical).
limits: No single-subject simultaneous multi-modal dataset currently available in open literature.

name: Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) Cross-Validation Algorithm Demonstration on Synthetic Benchmarks
design: Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation comparing Franke 2020 (calf) vs Rehman 2024 (quadriceps) against null mean baseline and standard monoexponential Kemp model.
limits: Evaluated on synthetic exponential curves generated via np.random.RandomState. LOSO across single-subject cohorts is strictly prohibited. Real empirical human out-of-sample cross-subject validation remains BLOCKED_PENDING_RAW_DATA.

name: SUBJECT-01 Integration: Functional Power, Recovery Limits, and TARGET-CPE45 Boundaries
design: Rigorous physical separation of external mechanical work (250 W * 2700 s = 675 kJ), whole-body metabolic cost (~3375 kJ at eta_gross ~20%), whole-body ATP turnover (62.5 mol ATP), oxidative resynthesis (~3300 kJ, ESTIMATED_SCENARIO_BALANCE_NOT_MEASURED), anaerobic glycolysis (~75 kJ, ESTIMATED_SCENARIO_BALANCE_NOT_MEASURED), local single-muscle PCr buffer (0.1-0.6 kJ), and reaction enthalpy Delta_R H = 21 kJ/mol. Inferring >99% oxidative contribution solely by dividing single-muscle static PCr buffer by 45-min whole-body external work is strictly prohibited as a category error.

results.scenario_assumptions: Theoretical scenario balance calculated at assumed nominal gross efficiency eta_gross = 20% and standard literature endurance partitioning. Not empirically measured in CPE45.

limits: TARGET-CPE45 remains NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED. Biological interventions maintain NO_GO. Local single-muscle PCr buffer cannot predict whole-body endurance without an independent systemic cardiorespiratory model.

name: Rehman 2024 31P-MRS Real Data: Protocol Timing Reconstruction, Kinetics Sensitivity, Partial pH Audit, and Within-Subject Model Transfer
design: Execution of comprehensive scientific validation suite on primary real human 31P-MRS time-series (Rehman 2024 Dryad Raw V3, 222 spectra, N=1 biological subject, 3 trials). Corrigendum incorporates: (1) Protocol timing audit separating inferred nominal cues (48-90s, INFERRED_TIMING_ASSUMPTION) from actual spectral nadir (144s in T1, 108s in T2/T3, OBSERVED_SPECTRAL_MINIMUM_DISTINCT_FROM_MECHANICAL_STOP) with verified PCr amplitudes; (2) Sensitivity analysis of recovery kinetics to onset shifts (-18s to +18s), quantifying systematic phase-selection uncertainty vs statistical error; (3) Rigorous investigation of -0.055 pH offset without ad-hoc empirical fudge factors (PH_CALIBRATION_PARTIAL) and formal retraction of pH >= 6.86 claim as superseded (calculated range 6.7932-7.0228); (4) Frozen model comparison: M0 (null constant baseline, negative R2), M1 (empirical 3-parameter monoexponential), M2 (reclassified as CONSTRAINED_MONOEXPONENTIAL_BASELINE), and M3 (full physiological ODE, M3_NOT_EXECUTABLE_ON_AVAILABLE_OBSERVATIONS); (5) Clear distinction between Scenario A (CONDITIONAL_TRAJECTORY_RECONSTRUCTION, mean transfer R2 = 0.8566) and Scenario B (PROSPECTIVE_PREDICTION_BLOCKED_UNOBSERVED_DEPLETION_DYNAMICS); (6) Numerical reconciliation of all report values with canonical JSON and preservation of TARGET-CPE45 freeze.

results.ph_retraction: pH >= 6.86 throughout retracted as superseded; Trial 1 min pH = 6.7932
identifiable_parameters: calculated_ph_dynamics (range 6.7932 to 7.0228, non-acidotic claim retracted as superseded)
unidentifiable_parameters: systemic_endurance_TARGET_CPE45 (localized knee kick cannot validate 45-min whole-body endurance)

limits: Dataset provides N=1 biological participant (3 repeated trials of localized single-leg knee extensions). Enables within-subject technical test-retest reproducibility and local rate parameter transfer, but strictly cannot validate cross-subject population variance or systemic 45-minute multi-muscle endurance (TARGET-CPE45).

name: PhysioNet ACTES Cycloergometer Multi-Subject Graded CPET: Strict Leave-One-Subject-Out Cross-Validation of Macroscopic Aerobic Coupling (N=18)
design: First independent multi-subject empirical validation of SUBJECT-01 macroscopic aerobic bioenergetic models on PhysioNet ACTES cycloergometer dataset (DOI 10.13026/2qs3-kh43, 52,062 synchronized beat-to-beat records across N=18 adolescent athletes). Strictly pre-registered and frozen parameters (eta_gross in [0.18, 0.28], c_ox = 20,900 J/L, tau = 35.0 s). Strict Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation across all 18 participants with zero test outcome leakage. Model comparison: M0 (null mean), M1 (empirical static linear), M2 Pop (dynamic first-order ODE with physiological delay), and M2 Allometric (dynamic ODE with body-mass normalization). Parameter identifiability analysis mapping observable macro-metabolic parameters vs strictly unidentifiable micro-compartment states.
limits: Validates macroscopic aerobic coupling (P_mech -> pulmonary VO2) and cardiorespiratory delay (tau = 35 s) across N=18 subjects. Apparent ramp delta efficiency eta_apparent = 37.49% reflects unlagged ramp slope; true steady-state delta efficiency is not identifiable from continuous ramp CPET. Identifies heterogeneous mass degradation in 7/18 subjects. Strictly cannot validate localized intracellular high-energy phosphates ([PCr], [Pi], [ATP]), cytosolic pH, motor unit recruitment rates, or 45-min constant extreme stress (TARGET-CPE45).

name: PhysioNet Malaga Treadmill CPET: Subject-Level Grouped Locomotion Kinetics, Substrate Oxidation, and Cross-Modality Transfer Barrier (N=981 valid tests, N=846 subjects)
design: Independent multi-subject empirical validation of SUBJECT-01 macroscopic cardiorespiratory models on PhysioNet Malaga Treadmill CPET dataset (DOI 10.13026/7ezk-j442, 575,087 breath-by-breath records across N=992 tests on N=857 human participants; N=981 valid incremental tests on N=846 unique participants admitted post-filtering). Evaluates: 1) Cryptographic verification of raw files against official SHA256SUMS.txt; 2) Epistemic classification of gas exchange (VO2, VCO2, RER measured) and derived oxycaloric model (46.8% RER > 1 analyzed as respiratory buffering/hyperventilation, not carbohydrate oxidation > 100%; true non-steady-state energy expenditure not independently validated); 3) 5-fold subject-level GroupKFold cross-validation across N=846 unique human participants (N=981 valid incremental tests) with guaranteed zero subject leakage; 4) Retention of legacy test-level split labeled with leakage risk; 5) Reclassification of naive cycling transfer into AD_HOC_CROSS_MODAL_MAPPING_FAILURE and setting PHYSICAL_CROSS_MODAL_TRANSFER_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE; 6) Rectification of apparent delta efficiency arithmetic in ACTES (37.49% apparent unlagged ramp slope, not true steady-state delta efficiency 25.5%, delta efficiency unidentifiable from unlagged ramp); 7) Maintenance of epistemic invariants (TARGET-CPE45 NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED, biological interventions strictly NO_GO).
limits: Validates macroscopic Phase II pulmonary cardiorespiratory ODE kinetics across treadmill running in N=846 independent human participants (N=981 valid tests) under guaranteed zero-leakage GroupKFold. Establishes ad-hoc cross-modality failure NEG-0037 and unidentifiability of physical cross-modality transfer due to lack of running mechanical work rate. Does not observe intracellular phosphates or validate 45-min critical power survivability.

name: Human In Vivo Vastus Lateralis Force, Activation Decoupling, and 20-Min Fatigue Dynamics (Bird 2026)
design: Empirical raw data acquisition, cryptographic verification, independent reproduction, and cross-subject Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) validation on Bird et al. (2026) multi-modal study (Dryad DOI 10.5061/dryad.sbcc2frmh, Science Robotics DOI 10.1126/scirobotics.aed5865, arXiv:2510.20866). Acquired and verified 4 priority raw archives: DATA_Isometric_Knee.xlsx (19,879 bytes), LME_Data_Outputs.mat (40,628 bytes), DATA_Dynamic_Knee.mat (5,212,093 bytes), and LSTM_Data_Outputs.zip (8,939,260 bytes). Independently reproduced author LME radar (R2 = 0.9844 +/- 0.0046, NRMSE = 3.28%) and LSTM fatigue (R2 = 0.9882 +/- 0.0059, RMSE = 2.74%) metrics. Executed cross-subject LOSO across N=6 participants, revealing that UWB radar collapses on unseen subjects (R2 = -2.4457 +/- 2.0154), while physiological M1 sEMG generalizes with R2 = 0.4628 +/- 0.0594 and M4 SUBJECT-01 achieves R2 = 0.3251 +/- 0.0863.
limits: Raw binary arrays DATA_Dynamic_Knee.mat (5.2 MB, 3,226 rows; torque in fraction of MVC [0.0, 1.0], partitioned into 1,382 passive protocol and 1,844 active protocol observations), DATA_Isometric_Knee.xlsx (19.9 KB), LME_Data_Outputs.mat (40.6 KB), and LSTM_Data_Outputs.zip (8.9 MB) are acquired and SHA256-verified. Only 681 MB DATA_Fatiguing_Isometric_Knee.xlsx remains pending due to upstream Dryad bot-protection gating. Cross-subject Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation on raw dynamic data demonstrates that the specific uncalibrated UWB Ridge model collapses (R2 = -2.4457 +/- 2.2077, NEG-0039), persisting across 15 sensitivity suite variations; this collapse is specific to the linear Ridge implementation and not extrapolated to non-linear architectures without dedicated LOSO validation. Tested engineered composite feature M4 (R2 = 0.3251) yields no statistically significant benefit over Hill model M3 (Delta R2 = +0.0148, p = 0.3294, which does not prove equivalence); sample point estimate favors baseline sEMG M1 (R2 = 0.4628, Delta R2 = -0.1377), but this difference is not statistically significant at alpha=0.05 (paired t = -2.462, p = 0.0571; Wilcoxon p = 0.0625; 95% CI [-0.2814, +0.0061]) due to limited power (N=6). Designated ENGINEERED_FEATURE_M4_NO_VERIFIED_ADVANTAGE; the full multiscale physiological ODE architecture of SUBJECT-01 remains unfalsified (FULL_SUBJECT01_MULTISCALE_ARCHITECTURE_NOT_FALSIFIED_BY_THIS_TEST). Single-joint dynamometer torque cannot be extrapolated to whole-body maximum strength or continuous 45-min endurance (TARGET-CPE45, NEG-0038). TARGET-CPE45 remains NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED and biological interventions strictly NO_GO.

name: Functional Biomechanical Multi-Muscle Bridge and Augmentation Feasibility Under Dynamic Antagonist Co-Activation
design: Multi-muscle quadriceps biomechanical force transmission modeling (PCSA weighting across Vastus Lateralis, Vastus Medialis, Vastus Intermedius, and Rectus Femoris), dynamic antagonist hamstring co-activation modeling (gamma = 0.08 + 0.14 * a_VL), strict 0-leakage Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation across N=6 human participants (3,226 dynamic observations from Bird et al. 2026 raw array DATA_Dynamic_Knee.mat), and TARGET-FORCE20 (+20% fiber force) augmentation feasibility simulation analyzing pennation angle hypertrophy penalty and patellar tendon tensile stress.
limits: Same-cohort Bird LOSO, six participants, normalized torque in fraction of MVC. In active protocols the bridge mean fold R2 is -0.1148 versus -0.0528 for sEMG. Modeled augmentation, pennation, stress and UTS-based ratios are scenario outputs. Tissue safety, measured augmentation and cross-cohort functional transfer remain unverified.

name: Portfolio evidence consolidation and read-only endpoint verification
design: Candidate screening, checksum-bound re-extraction of five derived outcomes, raw Bird active-only and mixed LOSO replay, configured scenario arithmetic, and grouped Malaga ad hoc transfer replay.
limits: Local derived evidence re-extraction is separate from full upstream pipeline replication. Bird and Malaga replay use the same original cohorts. No intervention efficacy or new functional validation.

name: E1: Independent Human Functional Strength Validation & Antagonist Co-Activation Transfer Audit
design: Systematic multi-repository data audit and locked pre-registration protocol comparing 5 torque prediction models (M0-M4) under uncalibrated (Regime A) and pre-calibrated (Regime B) LOSO transfer.
limits: DATA_BLOCKED: No public human dataset provides synchronized dynamometer active knee torque, MVC, and simultaneous surface EMG from both knee extensors and knee flexors across independent individuals.

name: E2: Tendon Regional Mechanics Validation & Segmental Morphometry Audit
design: Evaluation of regional vs uniform CSA strain prediction under invariant linear elastic material law; proof of literature mean substitution bias; separate ex vivo strength and fatigue failure analysis.
limits: DATA_BLOCKED: No open dataset provides synchronized participant-specific regional CSA (proximal, mid, distal) paired with local regional strain measurements and applied tendon load across independent individuals.

name: E5: Third Independent Human MTJ Cohort Replication & Myonuclear Program Audit
design: Systematic audit of MTJCore replication history (Stages 5, 6, 7); correlation-preserving null model pre-registration; global transcriptomic repository audit across ArrayExpress, GEO, and GSA-Human.
limits: DATA_BLOCKED: No third independent, publicly accessible human adult musculotendinous junction transcriptomic dataset exists outside the Copenhagen research group.

name: E1-ISO: Independent Human Isometric Knee Strength & Antagonist sEMG Validation
design: Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) 20-fold cross-validation of 5 nested regression models (M0-M4) on DPValid dataset (20 healthy adults, 125 extension and 121 flexion trials) testing whether antagonist sEMG improves torque estimation over agonist-only models.
limits: Isometric contractions only; dynamic isokinetic trials reserved for E1-DYN.

name: E2-REG: In Vivo Achilles Tendon Regional Displacement and Strain Analysis
design: High-frame-rate ultrasound speckle tracking analysis of intra-tendinous displacement and strain across superficial, middle, and deep layers in 10 healthy adults (160 observations) under passive rotation and isometric plantarflexion.
limits: Regional CSA not measured; mechanical stress cannot be computed. Designated as E2-REGIONAL-STRAIN.

name: E5-OXFORD-MTJ: Oxford Human Achilles Single-Cell Atlas Microanatomy Audit
design: Systematic cell-type and spatial transcriptomic audit of Cohen et al. (2026) single-cell atlas of human Achilles microanatomy to evaluate feasibility of replicating the Karlsen MTJCore gene program.
limits: Only stromal fibroblasts/tenocytes profiled; skeletal muscle myonuclei excluded.

name: E1-ABLATION: Factorial Feature Ablation of Anthropometrics and Multichannel sEMG in Torque Modeling
design: Full 2x5 factorial ablation (OLS, Ridge) across 5 nested feature sets (F0-F4) in 20-fold Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation on 125 extension trials (DPValid) to isolate true predictive sources.
limits: Isometric trials only; dynamic contractions require E1-DYN.

name: E2-CORRECTION: Subject-Level Nonparametric Statistical Re-Analysis & Pseudoreplication Correction
design: Independent biological participant aggregation (N=10) of Bogaerts et al. (2017) ultrasound speckle tracking data, correcting pseudoreplication in the Friedman test and evaluating between-limb correlation.
limits: Reproduction and statistical correction only; mechanical stress blocked by absent layer CSA.

name: E5-REASSESSMENT: Oxford Achilles Single-Cell Atlas Microanatomy & Stromal Specialization Audit
design: Forensic audit of Cohen et al. (2026) single-cell atlas and Mendeley Data repositories, resolving presence of muscle tissue and establishing exact criteria for MTJCore replication blockage.
limits: Myonuclear replication blocked by missing donor pseudobulk matrix in primary tables.

name: Oxford Achilles Atlas Data Recovery and MTJCore Discovery Identity Audit
design: Cross-repository audit of Oxford Achilles Atlas across Mendeley, CELLxGENE, GitHub, and HCA, verifying cell populations, counts, and proven identity with the MTJCore discovery cohort.
limits: Dataset was the original discovery cohort of MTJCore; circular re-evaluation prohibited.

name: Re-evaluation of Stromal-Myonuclear Dual Synthesis (HYP-0013)
design: Quantification of differential expression for MTJ components in myonuclear and fibroblast compartments; donor-consistency stress test and novelty audit.
limits: Transcriptomic abundance in snRNA-seq does not demonstrate extracellular secretion or mechanical force resistance.

name: Human Muscle Specific Tension Identification and Isomass Architectural Scaling Scenarios
design: Direct identification of human quadriceps specific tension sigma across N=20 adults (DPValid), LOSO CV of predictive models M0-M4, and theoretical isomass scaling simulations of force-velocity-ROM trade-offs under fixed muscle volume.
limits: Specific tension identified from in vivo voluntary dynamometry with allometric PCSA scaling; intracellular cross-bridge kinetics not directly imaged.

name: Tendon S-N Fatigue Life Modeling and +20% Force Augmentation Safety Envelope
design: Empirical calibration of Wöhler power-law fatigue parameters on human tendon mechanical data, and quantitative evaluation of safety factors and fatigue life under unadapted (+20% load, S1) and adaptive hypertrophic/remodeling (S2) augmentation scenarios.
limits: Fatigue life modeled from calibrated human tendon Wöhler baselines; in vivo dynamic multi-million cycle testing under augmentation remains a theoretical safety envelope.

name: Transfer of Force Prediction to Bilateral Isometric Leg Press & 3-DOF Closed Kinematic Chain Compatibility
design: Programmatic admission audit of 6 candidate cohorts for bilateral isometric leg press, paired subject-cluster bootstrap (B=10,000) reference benchmark on DPValid (N=20, 125 trials), and physically closed 3-DOF sagittal lower-limb linear programming solver without pseudoinverse shortcuts.
limits: Bilateral isometric leg press target cohort is DATA_BLOCKED (0/6 open candidates admitted). Closed-chain LP (Strategy 2 +21.64%) is MODEL_ONLY; DPValid paired bootstrap is a single-joint protocol-shift reference.

name: Tendon-Enthesis Multi-Layer Viscoelastic Shear Stress Under Rapid dF/dt and Remodeling Heterochrony Hazard
design: Calibration of superficial-to-deep displacement partitioning on Bogaerts et al. (2017, N=10), 3-layer Standard Linear Solid viscoelastic shear-lag enthesis stress solver across dF/dt in 2,000..25,000 N/s, and 168-day muscle-tendon adaptation heterochrony ODE.
limits: Viscoelastic shear-lag and 168-day collagen turnover ODE are MODEL_ONLY projections calibrated to group-level Bogaerts kinematics and Kongsgaard regional CSA without 3D transverse sub-tendon MRI.

name: Multi-Compartment Cylindrical Pennes Bioheat Transfer and Intermittent CPE45 Workload Envelope
design: 4-shell cylindrical Pennes bioheat + central arterial pool backward-Euler solver over 2700 s anchored to Malaga CPET (N=846) and ACTES metabolic rates, across intermittent duty cycles D in [0.15, 1.00], 4 ambient climates, AEGIS-01 barrier penalty, and tools/cpe45.py compatibility check.
limits: Thermoregulatory dynamics over 2700 s are MODEL_ONLY; TARGET-CPE45 remains NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED due to absence of empirical human post-45min functional trials.

name: Master Architecture A Integration and Canonical Specification Across Closed-Chain, Enthesis, and Thermal Constraints
design: Unified synthesis of DEC-0025 functional validation baselines with EXP-0061 (3-DOF chain & cohort audit), EXP-0062 (enthesis shear dF/dt & heterochrony), and EXP-0063 (Pennes bioheat CPE45 envelope) into Architecture A canonical specification and GO/HOLD/NO_GO adjudication matrix.
limits: Integrates empirical human anchors with MODEL_ONLY multi-physics coupling; does not substitute for empirical external validation of bilateral leg press or 2700 s endurance.

name: Archive replay and equal-external-work thermal controls
design: Replay EXP-0061–0064 in temporary outputs and compare published 360 W scenarios to constant equal-work controls at three integration steps and to a lumped storage model.
limits: Model-only comparison of fixed archived inputs; no causal functional effect or human thermal threshold is validated.

name: Frozen Pennes out-of-domain transfer to observed esophageal temperature
design: Compare the frozen solver with persistence for measured 5-min within-session esophageal temperature changes before fan exposure. Participant-cluster paired bootstrap and prespecified humidity sensitivity.
limits: 6 eligible participants and 35 sessions; protocol-assigned power and assumed humidity; light cycling only, no post45 or functional profile.

name: External thermal transfer on McLaughlin cycling cohort
design: Prespecified 1-to-45-minute rectal temperature change, frozen EXP-0063 model versus persistence and lumped heat model with participant bootstrap.
limits: 23 participants, constant initial power and 5–6 min environment; nominal thermal layer initialization, rectal endpoint; no direct CPE45 validation.

name: One-factor closed-chain sensitivity
design: One-factor perturbation of friction, COP, plate angle, height and common specific tension in EXP-0061 at two postures.
limits: Static model only, one-factor conditional grids, no tendon constraints and no external leg-press observations.

name: Static chain to conditional tendon stress coupling
design: Map archived single-limb quadriceps torque to tendon force using the existing moment arm, then sweep CSA, UTS and loading rate under EXP-0062 stress assumptions.
limits: Static moment-derived tendon force, assumed loading rate and tissue parameters, no dynamic or in-vivo validation.

name: Controlled adaptation-rate comparison
design: Replay EXP-0062 and compare muscle time constants 16, 12.8 and 12 days with identical tendon parameters and daily loading.
limits: Conditional model with assumed tissue adaptation and fatigue curve; no human adaptation efficacy or injury risk measured.

name: Fujii resting drift and initial thermal sensitivity
design: Exploratory pre-exercise 270-second esophageal changes compared with frozen solver nominal and uniform layer initialization at zero and nominal power.
limits: Six participants, 24 sessions, exploratory analysis after previous test, assumed initial temperatures and rest metabolism. No CPE45 endpoint.

name: Initial thermal-state sensitivity on previously viewed McLaughlin cohort
design: Compare nominal and uniform initial layer temperatures using the same previously viewed participants, outcome and input assumptions as EXP-0067.
limits: Retrospective reuse of EXP-0067 cohort; initial layer temperatures unmeasured, humidity and workload assumptions unchanged. No CPE45 validation.

name: Audit McLaughlin power and climate time series
design: Audit power 1–45 minutes and sparse climate on EXP-0067 cohort; numerically labelled rows interpreted post hoc as interval end.
limits: Exploratory reuse, numeric timestamps interpreted as interval ends pending author confirmation; no temperature replay.

name: Variable-input thermal replay on McLaughlin cohort
design: Replay EXP-0067 with minute-resolved recorded power, timestamp shifts and sparse step-held environment; compare participant-paired errors.
limits: Previously viewed cohort, numeric timestamps interpreted as interval ends pending author confirmation; fixed initialization and climate assumptions, no CPE45 measurement.

name: Held-subject late sprint power and cross-protocol transfer
design: Compare first-sprint persistence and first-two-sprint linear regression for tenth sprint using participant LOSO within Chmura and Jutlah, plus Chmura-to-Jutlah transfer.
limits: Previously examined cohorts, first two measured efforts required, Chmura climate pairing unknown, different rest protocols. No direct biochemical recovery or CPE45 validation.

name: Paired cognitive reaction and accuracy after cycling
design: Participant-paired exercise-versus-rest changes in correct response latency and accuracy on three Stroop conditions, 10000 participant bootstrap samples.
limits: Post-exercise aggregated cognitive reaction outcomes, no trial-level omissions, movement trajectory, 45-minute protocol or architecture effect. No predefined equivalence bounds.

name: Conditional static-chain tendon and thermal interface
design: Join archived static chain and tendon proxy to a shared prescribed 2700-second external-power profile under fixed mass and environment; report unavailable functional channels.
limits: Conditional interface only: static force is not a dynamic trajectory, prescribed power is not coupled to fatigue; motor and post45 unmeasured.

name: Torque-to-tendon interface sensitivity
design: Diagnostic grid of post-LP tendon moment arm, CSA, UTS and force rate; solve arm multiplier at model SF 1.5.
limits: Moment arm varied only after LP with fixed torque, no anatomically self-consistent re-optimization or tissue safety validation.

name: Closed-chain moment arm reoptimization
design: Re-solve EXP-0061 LP with quadriceps arm multipliers 0.8–1.2 and use the same arm to compute EXP-0069 tendon proxy.
limits: Static model, common arm scaling, assumed tissue properties and loading rate. No individual in vivo validation or CPE45.

name: Held-participant retrospective leg-press velocity loss
design: Participant-weighted leave-one-person-out linear velocity loss versus completed-set percentage compared with constant, bootstrap by participant.
limits: Completed-set percentage requires future information; missing early rows, one group and protocol, no force or tissue measurements, no prospective external validation.

name: Held-participant squat moment model and load transfer
design: Train constant, angle and angle-plus-velocity linear models on 0 lb with held participants, test on both 0 lb and 25 lb; bootstrap participant MAE difference.
limits: One cohort, moment derived from inverse dynamics, unresolved moment scaling ISS-0028, no augmentation or maximum force.

name: Independent OpenSim reconstruction for squat moment scale
design: Reconstruct IK and ID from two subject models, markers and ground forces; compare held source moments against Nm and Nm/kg scale hypotheses with prespecified gates.
limits: Two subjects, exact author ID configuration unknown, discrepancy in AB02. No resolution of source moment units or human augmentation.

name: Squat force provenance and platform moment sensitivity
design: Compare exported and force-plate vertical forces on aligned frames, then recompute inverse dynamics with all platform moments or vertical-only moments and report four frame masks.
limits: Two previously inspected participants, scenario B assumes an unverified convention for plate moments; no physical validation or biological effects.

name: Held-participant transfer of conditional squat moment reconstruction
design: Prespecified vertical-only versus all platform moments on AB03 and AB06; primary unloaded squat, secondary 25 lb; reconstruct IK/ID and compare same-time source moment.
limits: Same cohort, model-derived outcome, two held participants, broad threshold, AB03 differs 26.6%, convention and tissue effects unverified; weight condition may omit external hand load.

name: Couple recovery energy ledger, thermal solver and conditional force interface
design: Run corrected D2 on 27 60s/40s cycles at assumed fatigue rates; transfer its output and ledger heat to Pennes at 1 and 0.5 s, compare same-power heat formula, attach explicit static force/tendon proxies.
limits: D2 failed prior transfer; fatigue-to-force and heat allocation are hypothetical, no thermal feedback, tissue damage, motor function or post45, no in-vivo efficacy inference.

name: McLaughlin 60-minute thermal trajectory with power input
design: Retrospective full 60–1 minute and late 60–45 minute rectal-temperature changes; compare variable and constant power Pennes, persistence, and individual-mass lumped comparator.
limits: Previously reviewed same cohort; assumed power timestamps and early climate; lumped predicts mean body, outcome rectal; no post45 function, new cohort or CPE45 validation.

name: Scoped external bilateral isometric force cohort and adaptation trajectory
design: Compare fixed EXP-0061 100-degree nominal force against participant-held-out W0 cohort mean for Santos ~110-degree leg press; bootstrap participant MAE, describe W0-POS paired changes.
limits: Eleven men, angle/device differ, no subject mass or geometry, no parallel control and one W3 label unexplained. Does not validate exact EXP-0061 or functional enhancement.

name: Hip parameter audit and exploratory 110-degree force transfer
design: AST and numerical hip-parameter invariance over all scenarios, then fixed-geometry knee 110-degree LP versus prior 100-degree and LOSO force reference on reused Santos W0.
limits: Hip parameter invariant because unused, not physiology; knee-only post hoc comparison uses same 11 participants and ignores individual geometry; no whole-system validation.

name: Gravity derivative finite-difference audit and corrected chain sensitivity
design: Compare central finite differences of documented segment potential against original and corrected hip gravity terms at three knee poses; re-solve archived LP with one correction and recompute conditional tendon proxy.
limits: Arithmetic within stated potential; one-line in-memory change; unmeasured hip/trunk geometry, muscle function, tissue and whole-system efficacy remain unvalidated.

name: Controlled rebuild of gravity-dependent model scenarios
design: Replay archived model, apply one verified hip gravity correction in memory, rebuild 0064/0068/0069/0077–0079/0085 outputs and compare provenance, cases, energy and model-only gates.
limits: Gravity-only correction; same unvalidated hip geometry, tendon assumptions and recovery model. Later empirical comparisons not rebuilt; no new physiological or architecture validation.

name: Gravity-corrected chain comparison on reused Santos force cohort
design: Recalculate paired W0 MAE and bias using archived and gravity-corrected 100- and 110-degree nominal forces versus LOSO mean, with participant bootstrap.
limits: Reused data, model geometry mismatched and not individualized; no independent external validation or architecture effect.

name: Gravity-corrected leg-press chord-direction sensitivity
design: Rerun corrected chain on prespecified five chord directions and three knee angles; inspect tendon proxy and reused Santos W0 force versus LOSO.
limits: Diagnostic chord grid, not individual hip posture; reused Santos data, tendon proxy, no whole architecture or real functional assessment.
